instagram_check.note: No confirmed Instagram business account found. The only IG hit for this exact business name is an Instagram LOCATION TAG page (not a business profile) showing 2 unrelated stock photos (a schnauzer studio portrait and a Presidio Equine horse-riding ad) auto-attached by Instagram's geotag system, not this salon's own content. rating_source: Google, via two independent snapshots that agree on the star value (4.6) and disagree only on the review count, which is expected since counts grow over time: (1) dogdog.org embeds a LIVE Google Maps widget keyed to Google Place ID ChIJM33al9zA2YgR52_G-UDiGIY; this session's own WebFetch/curl of that page (2026-07-23) independently found an aria-label 'Rating: 4.5 out of 5' with a title attribute of '4.6' (Google's widget renders aria-label rounded to the nearest 0.5 but keeps the precise decimal in the title attribute) alongside the text '151 people rated this'. (2) Birdeye's review-aggregation page for this business shows an explicit per-source breakdown: 'Google: 167 reviews, Yellow Pages: 9 reviews' (176 total), with an overall 4.6 rating. This site's headline figure (4.6 / 167) uses Birdeye's Google-specific breakdown as the larger/more recent Google snapshot, with dogdog.org's 151 kept here as a corroborating, slightly older Google snapshot, and the Birdeye combined total (176, Google+Yellow Pages) and Yelp's separate count (48-49 reviews per Yelp's own page title and two independent mirror sites, giftly.com showing 4.3/48) also disclosed for transparency. A third figure surfaced only in an AI-generated WebSearch overview ('4.6 stars, 73 reviews', attributed to ourpetgroomer.com) could not be traced to a primary source on that page and was NOT used. All figures (151, 167, 176, 48-49) comfortably clear the pipeline's rating>=4.5 and reviews>=10 filter regardless of which is used; none of the discrepancy affects the pass/fail decision, only which headline number is most defensible, so 4.6/167 (Google via Birdeye) was chosen as the most Google-specific, most recent figure available.

hours.note: Monday-Saturday 9am-4pm / Sunday closed is the majority reading, corroborated independently by dogdog.org, the WebSearch AI overview (citing task-brief-style aggregation) and the original task brief context. One outlier, wheree.com, instead shows 'Monday closed, Tuesday-Saturday 9am-5pm, Sunday closed' -- a single dissenting source against three converging ones, so the majority version (Mon-Sat 9-4, Sun closed) was used on-site and in JSON-LD, with this discrepancy disclosed here for transparency.

founded: 2004 (per Yelp, dogdog.org, businessyab and multiple independent mirrors, all consistently citing 2004 as the year established; used on-site as '20+ years' / 'family-run since 2004').

services_source: No published price list found anywhere: no owned website, no booking platform, and no directory checked in this session shows itemized current prices. One historical data point was found (Groupon deal page, via WebSearch summary only, direct fetch blocked 403): a past deal listed 'complete grooming, small dog under 20lbs, $45 value' and 'medium dog up to 30lbs, $55 value'. This is dated/promotional pricing tied to specific weight tiers, not a current general price list, so it was NOT rendered on the site (site uses 'Call for pricing' throughout, per PIPELINE.md and the output/angels-have-paws-tallahassee precedent for businesses with no published price list); recorded here only for internal transparency.

images.curation_note: Every candidate photo (13 total across both sources) was opened and viewed individually before selection, per PIPELINE.md fase 3 visual curation rule. No blurry photos, no visible clutter, no uncomfortable-looking pets, no owner/staff portraits used as gallery tiles. 8 final photos used across hero + experience + gallery, all showing real dogs groomed at this specific salon (5 with the salon's own logo overlay as direct evidence) plus 2 real candid outdoor moments and the real business logo.

brand_vibe: Playful, warm and family-friendly. The real business logo (sampled directly via PIL pixel sampling from the actual photos) is a bright teal/turquoise box (~#48bfa3) with a smiling golden-yellow cartoon dog mascot (~#f9d038) and a red heart, white 'A Labor of Love / Dog Grooming' wordmark. The salon's own customer photos are framed in bright orange/marigold polka-dot borders (~#ffae1e / ~#e27010) from the photo-collage app used to post them. Base kept LIGHT/warm cream to match the friendly, approachable feel; accent built around a vivid pumpkin-orange (from the recurring collage borders) with the brand teal as a secondary accent, both distinct from every palette already listed as used in DESIGN.md ('esmeralda', 'teal acero', 'coral fairy', 'caramelo', 'violeta dark', 'rosa dark', 'gold dark').
base_template: templates/light-v2 (light base, lashbloom exemplar, EN default)

palette.derivation: accent_deep and accent_mid are a pumpkin-orange / warm-gold pair matching the recurring orange collage borders and the golden dog mascot found across the business's real customer photos. bg is a warm cream, bg_2 a pale mint-cream tying to the brand's teal logo without repeating any already-used DESIGN.md palette. All other gradient/shadow/orb tokens in the CSS were remapped from the lashbloom exemplar's pink-family palette to this orange/teal/cream family, preserving each original token's relative lightness so every gradient and shadow still reads correctly (see scripts/build_aloveofloredoggroomingkendall.py HEX_PALETTE/RGBA_PALETTE tables for the full 26-hex + 9-rgba mapping).

jsonld_type_note: Used @type: LocalBusiness. schema.org has no formally valid pet-grooming-specific type, so LocalBusiness was used as the safe, always-valid choice, consistent with output/angels-have-paws-tallahassee.
build_method: Anchored transformation script (Python, rep()/rep_all() with assert-before-replace, plus 2 whole-block regex replacements for the services grid and gallery grid) over templates/light-v2/index.html per templates/SKELETONS-V2.md, in scripts/build_aloveofloredoggroomingkendall.py. index.html was never written from scratch; the script always starts from a fresh copy of the pristine template.

manual_visual_qa: Rendered the built site locally with Playwright (headless Chromium) and screenshotted every section in both EN (default) and ES (toggle), plus manually forced the .reveal/.img-reveal/.split IntersectionObserver classes to confirm all 8 real photos decode and display correctly, the palette and motion system render as intended, and the bilingual toggle swaps every string correctly (including the untranslated review quotes staying in English as required). Confirmed the pristine, unmodified templates/light-v2/index.html exhibits the exact same 'reveal classes never trigger under fast programmatic scrollTo in headless automation' behavior, i.e. not a regression introduced by this build.
